stories.headline: UNISON: handover delays harming patients and crews
stories.body: In a UNISON survey of 654 ambulance staff in England, 59% said patients got worse while waiting to be handed over and 7% had cared for someone for 12 hours. 34% are thinking of leaving.
stories.why: Handover delays aren't just a target issue: they affect patient safety and whether colleagues stay.

stories.headline: NWAS renews paramedic apprenticeship with Cumbria
stories.body: A new five-year deal with the University of Cumbria keeps the route open for EMTs to train as paramedics while working. More than 600 NWAS staff have qualified this way since 2021, with teaching now at Lancaster and Liverpool Hope University.
stories.why: Earn-while-you-learn routes widen who can become a paramedic and help grow the workforce.

stories.headline: Some NIAS ambulance defibrillators have faults
stories.body: Some Corpuls3 defibrillators on NIAS double-crewed ambulances have intermittent module connection errors. Backup Zoll AED Pros are being put on board while power boards are replaced. No patient harm has been found.
stories.why: Most faults were caught on daily vehicle checks, a reminder of why those checks matter.

stories.headline: SECAmb plans £24.8m Make Ready Centre in Farnborough
stories.body: Guildford-area crews would start and end shifts at a hub where specialist teams clean and restock vehicles, working from local response posts in between. Tongham and Haslemere stations are under review; no closures have been announced.
stories.why: Make Ready models change how crews start shifts and where they are based day to day.

stories.headline: Scaffolder meets EMAS crew who saved him after 12 shocks
stories.body: A Northamptonshire scaffolder went into cardiac arrest at home and arrested again after prolonged CPR and 12 defibrillator shocks. His friend's CPR, guided by a call handler, bought vital time, and he has now met his lifesavers.
stories.why: Bystander CPR and call-handler support give crews a fighting chance.
